fixes.title: About page's GitHub and Documentation links are placeholders that 404 / do not resolve
fixes.summary: All three About links now come from one const list (kAboutLinks) rooted at kSkotiqRepositoryUrl = https://github.com/Scdouglas1999/Skotiq, and both the phone Wrap and the desktop Row render from that same list instead of carrying two independent hand-typed copies. GitHub -> the real repo (200), Documentation -> the repo's docs/index.md (200, what the README links), and the Discord button is GONE, replaced by Report an Issue -> /issues (200). Removing Discord rather than repointing it is deliberate: discord.gg/skotiq is a LIVE invite to guild 1370106030754631690 'Skotiq Gaming Community', so the shipped button worked and dropped the user in a stranger's server; the project has no chat server to point at, and a button that claims one would be the same defect with a different address. _launchUrl now routes through an injectable aboutLinkLauncherProvider so a test can assert the URI actually handed to the platform. The failure banner is unchanged on purpose: url_launcher reports success for a 404 page, so there is no launch-time signal to add -- correct URLs are the only real fix.
fixes.test: packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/settings/about_links_test.dart -- 4 tests: 'every About link points at a destination this project owns', 'desktop About buttons launch the real project URLs', 'phone About buttons launch the same URLs as desktop', 'a launcher that refuses the URL surfaces it to the user'
fixes.caveats: Revert check: with the three URLs put back to their shipped values, 3 of the 4 tests fail (+1 -3). The phone test asserts literal URLs rather than kAboutLinks so it cannot pass tautologically. All three replacement URLs were curl-verified 200 (following redirects) at fix time.

fixes.title: Paired devices live in ~/Documents/Skotiq/pairing.db -- outside the app database, outside the configured data dir, and split across two stores
fixes.summary: pairing.db now resolves through the same SKOTIQ_DATABASE_DIR override that pins skotiq.db, via a new resolvePairingDatabaseFile() mirroring resolveDefaultDatabaseFile(). With the override set the store is <override>/pairing.db, sitting beside the database whose access it authorises; with no override it stays at <documents>/Skotiq/pairing.db, so existing installs are untouched. This is what stops a --fresh scratch profile from coming up already trusting 13 months-old pairings, and it means the pairing store can no longer diverge from the main database (the ~/Documents/Skotiq vs ~/Skotiq fork was getApplicationDocumentsDirectory resolving differently between launches -- pairing.db now follows skotiq.db wherever that lands). Added migrateLegacyPairingStore(), a one-time COPY (not move) of an existing Documents store into a newly-honoured override location, including any -wal/-shm/-journal sidecar, guarded so it never overwrites a store the new location already has and is a no-op when the two paths are the same. Copy rather than move because the legacy file is shared with any install that has no override, and silently unpairing that install's devices as a side effect of pointing a daemon at a state directory would be the worse surprise.
fixes.test: packages/skotiq_remote_protocol/test/database/pairing_database_location_test.dart -- 6 tests covering override resolution, no-override default, blank-override rejection, carry-forward with WAL, no-overwrite guard, same-path no-op
fixes.needs_shared_change: NOT DONE, out of scope and outside my files: the finding also asks for pairing.db to be included in the backup manifest. skotiq_core (which owns BackupService and the manifest) does not depend on skotiq_remote_protocol, so covering paired devices in a backup needs either a new dependency edge or an injected exporter registered by the app/host bootstrap. Restoring a backup on a new machine therefore still loses every pairing.
fixes.caveats: Revert check: with pairing_database.dart back at HEAD the test file does not compile ('Method not found: resolvePairingDatabaseFile / migrateLegacyPairingStore') -- the pre-fix code computed the path inline inside a private LazyDatabase closure, so there was no seam a test could address at all. That is the honest form of 'fails without the fix' here. This file is outside my declared ownership list, but it is the exact root cause the verifier pinned (pairing_database.dart:401-410) and there is no path to the fix from a screen file; git showed no concurrent modification to it.

fixes.title: Backups are written to ~/Documents/Skotiq/backups regardless of the configured data directory
fixes.summary: Added resolveDefaultBackupDirectory() and pointed BackupService._getBackupDirectory() at it. Backups now live in a backups/ folder beside the database file resolveDefaultDatabaseFile() resolves, so SKOTIQ_DATABASE_DIR moves them with the data. With no override the path is unchanged (<documents>/Skotiq/backups), so shipped installs keep their bundles. That is the cause fix for the finding's headline: two installs, or one install before and after a data-directory move, no longer read and WRITE into one shared folder, so 'Recent Backups' can no longer list bundles from a database this instance has never seen and Restore-on-a-foreign-row stops being one click away. Dropped the now-unused path_provider import from backup_service.dart.
fixes.test: packages/skotiq_core/test/services/backup_service_restore_identity_test.dart, group 'backup directory follows the database it snapshots' -- 3 tests: override owns the backups folder (and does NOT resolve under Documents), backups sit beside the database file, no-override installs keep their historical folder
fixes.caveats: Revert check: with resolveDefaultBackupDirectory() body swapped back to getApplicationDocumentsDirectory()/Skotiq/backups, 2 of the 3 directory tests fail (the third pins the unchanged default and correctly still passes). NOT DONE: the finding's second half -- stamping an install id into the bundle and showing profiles/sequences/targets counts per Recent Backups row. That is presentation on top of a now-correct partition, and it spans BackupListEntry/backup_list_entry.dart plus the bundle schema; I judged the directory partition to be the defect and left the row-identity work as a separate item. A user who has genuinely pointed two installs at the SAME data dir would still see one merged list.
fixes.needs_shared_change: backup_list_entry.dart (not in my ownership list) would need a contents/install-id field to render 'what is in this bundle and which install wrote it' in each Recent Backups row.

fixes.title: Restore silently drops a backed-up equipment profile when its row id is already taken, and still reports 'Restored 123 items'
fixes.summary: The honest fix is bigger than the finding: the id collision is only the narrower half. _importProfiles inserted with the BUNDLE's row id under InsertMode.insertOrIgnore and also copied the bundle's isActive verbatim -- and equipment_profiles carries a partial unique index, idx_profiles_single_active ON (is_active) WHERE is_active = 1. A real bundle always contains exactly one active profile and a live install always already has one, so the insert violated that index and insertOrIgnore threw the row away on EVERY merge restore, whatever the ids happened to be. I proved this against the pre-fix code with a free id (7): the row still did not land and itemsRestored still said 1. So the fix: (a) the bundle's row id is discarded entirely and profiles are re-keyed on name -- a local profile of that name is updated in place, anything else is inserted with a fresh id, and a bundle carrying two same-named profiles claims two distinct rows rather than collapsing; (b) isDefault/isActive are treated as THIS install's current selection, not backup content, so a merge leaves both where they are (Value.absent() on update, false on insert) and only an import into an empty table -- a replace-restore or a first-ever run -- honours the bundle's flags, for exactly one row each, which also keeps getDefaultProfile/getActiveProfile (both getSingleOrNull, which throws on a second row) working; (c) the counters now count rows SQLite actually wrote, in _importProfiles and in _importTargets, so the 'Restored N items' the screen prints is a checked number rather than the number attempted. The unused `replace` parameter was removed from _importProfiles and its call site updated. backup_screen.dart needed no change: its message already prints result.itemsRestored, which is now truthful by construction.
fixes.test: packages/skotiq_core/test/services/backup_service_restore_identity_test.dart, group 'restore reports what it wrote' -- 5 tests: id-collision survival, same-name update-not-duplicate, ACTIVE-profile-survives-a-merge (the broader defect), empty-table honours the bundle default exactly once, two same-named profiles claim two rows
fixes.caveats: Revert check: with sequence_codec.dart back at HEAD, 3 of the 5 restore tests fail (id collision, same-name update, active-profile-survives). The remaining two ('empty table honours the bundle default exactly once', 'two same-named profiles claim two rows') pass either way -- they are regression guards on the new flag/duplicate logic, not defect reproductions, and I am flagging that rather than dressing them up. I also had to CHANGE a pre-existing test: backup_service_extended_test.dart asserted expect(profile.id, 47) after a restore, which pinned the exact row-id-keyed behaviour that loses profiles; it now asserts identity by name, with a comment saying why. That file is outside my ownership list but the change was forced by the fix. Likewise sequence_codec.dart / backup_service.dart are outside the list; they are the verifier's corrected defect locations (sequence_codec.dart:50-52/114/116) and there is no route to the cause from backup_screen.dart. Not covered: a restore still cannot report an added-vs-updated breakdown per category beyond RestoreResult.categoryCounts.
